title: Femoral Pediatric Fractures. Walking Spica Cast vs Synthetic Pants
brief_summary: Femoral pediatric shaft fractures are a common orthopedic injury. Conservative treatment is still the preferred method by orthopedic surgeons. The walking spica cast is used in patients between 1 year old and 6 years old, in patients with isolated and low-energy fractures. The use of synthetic materials is preferred (fiber glass) for resistance, durability and low weight makes them optimal.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Simple fractures (transverse or short oblique fracture)
* Less than 2 cm of shortening
* Independent walking ability
* Closed fractures
* Isolated shaft fractures
* Low energy
* Written informed consent by the parents

Exclusion Criteria:

* Polytraumatized patients
* Cranial trauma or spinal cord injury
* Articular extension of the fracture
* History of femoral shaft fracture
